In summary, our research is concerned with
distributed detection in which the observations are quantized into M-ary symbols and transmitted to a central fusion center.
the problem of distributed detection of signals in Gaussian noise.
the problem of designing a distributed detection system with a Neyman-Pearsonian constraint on the false-alarm probability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Neyman-Person performance of the identical-quantizer scheme is asymptotically as good as that of any system.
the Neyman-Peerason performance of the best identical- quantizer system is within an O(log n) factor of that achieved by an absolutely optimal system.
the performance degradation due to quantization is at most a constant multiple of the performance degradation due due to the loss of correlation between the quantized observations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the type-II error probability of the best identical quantizer system is bounded from above by a fixed (independent of n) multiple of the type-II error achieved by the absolutely-optimal system.
we have shown the optimality of the Neyman-Person parallel system under the condition that the number of quantizer levels is large enough.
we have shown how to achieve a fixed error probability for the Neyman-Peerason criterion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the distributed Neyman-Pearon problem is not sensitive to the number of sensors n.
the Neyman-Person performance of distributed detection systems is robust to quantization.
the Neyman-Person performance of a distributed detector with identical quantizers is within a fixed multiple of the performance of the optimal detector.
